# Engagement Overhaul Task List

Last updated: 2026-07-24

## End Goal Quick Answer

FORGE must be one deterministic authorized engagement pipeline from scoped
multi-seed intake through bounded recursive discovery, static artifact
enrichment, non-destructive validation-before-reporting, rule-engine
findings/severity, graph/dashboard/report/audit review, guaranteed template/raw
fallback when LLM/API narrative providers fail, and automated test-data cleanup.

This is the only active product goal. Every current task must implement, harden,
or test one of these gates: intake, discovery, recursion, artifact analysis,
validation, scoring, review, fallback, or testing/cleanup. Subagents and Claude
may accelerate execution or review, but they do not redefine the goal.

When context is low, answer the end-goal question from `END_GOAL.md` and this
section first, then choose the next task from `## Compact active backlog`.

## Operating model

- Goal lock: `FORGE-DETERMINISTIC-ASM-PIPELINE-v1`. Fast goal entry point: `END_GOAL.md`; root implementer spec: `SPEC.md`; compact workflow contract: `docs/deterministic_engagement_contract.md`; normative end-goal source: `docs/end_goal.md`. The `## Canonical End Goal` checklist below is acceptance criteria derived from that contract, not live completion status; if they conflict, update this checklist to match `docs/end_goal.md` before continuing. Current implementation order lives under `## Compact active backlog`.
- Current workspace status: this checkout is a Git repository on `main` tracking `origin/main`. Deep historical entries that say commits were impossible because the workspace was not a Git repo are stale context only; continue making meaningful commits and pushes when changes are valid.
- Historical backprop notes that say `No SPEC.md exists` are stale after
  2026-07-20. New goal, invariant, or bug-contract notes should update
  `SPEC.md` plus the active handoff docs.
- Live probing and tool execution are allowed when the engagement scope/config explicitly authorizes them. They must be bounded, logged, resumable, and tested with mocks or local fixtures unless a real target is explicitly provided for that run. Live `--attack-mode` and `--auto-run-detected` execution must carry `--roe-id`/`FORGE_ROE_ID` plus `--scope-manifest`/`FORGE_SCOPE_MANIFEST`; `FORGE_REQUIRE_SCOPE_MANIFEST=1` extends the manifest requirement to every non-dry-run kill-chain launch. Use `--dry-run` to preview without live execution.
- Default automation must not silently cross scope or perform destructive exploitation, password attacks, persistence, lateral movement, or post-exploitation actions.
- Subagents and Claude are review/execution accelerators, not competing
  source-of-truth docs. Use them for bounded independent review or disjoint work
  when available; if thread or turn caps block them, continue locally against the
  locked end-goal contract and record the limitation.

## Canonical End Goal

FORGE is a comprehensive, deterministic, authorized attack-surface management and threat-intelligence platform. It must start from one or more scoped engagement seeds, recursively discover public or explicitly authorized attack surface, statically analyze discovered artifacts, validate cloud and credential evidence non-destructively before reporting, calculate risk with deterministic rules, expose the engagement through graph/dashboard/report surfaces, and always generate auditable output even when LLM/API narrative providers fail, hit quota, have no key, or exceed token limits.

End-goal lock: the target is one reproducible authorized engagement pipeline,
not a loose backlog of scanners, providers, or UI polish. Every active task must
map to one of the deterministic acceptance stages in `docs/end_goal.md`:
intake, discovery, recursion, artifact analysis, validation, scoring, review,
fallback, or testing/cleanup.

Status semantics: these unchecked boxes are end-state acceptance criteria. They
are intentionally not a live task queue and should not override the current
continuation order in `## Compact active backlog`.

- [ ] Every scoped active probe, follow-on tool execution, and read-only credential/resource validation is gated by explicit ROE/scope manifest, bounded concurrency, deterministic depth/queue budgets, audit logging, and dry-run preview. Passive provider OSINT still stays scope-filtered, budgeted, logged, and provider-paced; `FORGE_REQUIRE_SCOPE_MANIFEST=1` can require a scope manifest for every non-dry-run launch.
- [ ] Multi-seed engagements support domains, IPs, URLs, emails, phones, usernames, company names, cloud refs, and artifact URLs under one auto-incrementing engagement record.
- [ ] Recursive discovery fans out across passive OSINT, identity enrichment, web mining, artifact parsing, cloud-reference detection, and explicitly authorized live checks.
- [ ] Cross-reference synthesis merges duplicate entities, promotes high-confidence secondary seeds, flags conflicts, and terminates deterministically when depth, queue, or stable-snapshot conditions are met.
- [ ] Static artifact analysis automatically handles mobile bundles, archives, configs, documents, mail containers, source/package metadata, Terraform/Helm/OCI/Docker-style artifacts, and other passive containers without executing them.
- [ ] Cloud and credential validation is non-destructive, proof-bound, placeholder/honeypot-aware, provider-respectful, and validation-before-reporting is enforced.
- [ ] Severity and report gates are deterministic rule-engine outputs only; LLMs may write narrative but cannot invent findings, alter severity, or weaken proof gates.
- [ ] Reporting always degrades through LLM cascade, local/template fallback, and raw JSON/CSV export with checksums and render-path metadata.
- [ ] Dashboard/detail pages expose engagement metadata, seeds, findings, graph exports, report history, validation inventory, raw exports, and hash-chain audit manifests.
- [ ] Acceptance requires focused tests, mocked end-to-end kill-chain tests, offline-strict tests, report fallback tests, validation gate tests, dashboard contract tests, and cleanup proving no test engagements remain.

## Current Execution End Goal

Do not treat this as a UI-only or checklist-polish effort. The current end goal
is a reproducible authorized kill-chain workflow that starts from a multi-seed
engagement, recurses through passive OSINT, identity, web, artifact,
cloud-reference, and explicitly authorized live-check fan-outs, validates
evidence non-destructively, emits deterministic findings/severity/graph/report
artifacts, renders the engagement for dashboard review, and leaves no automated
test engagement debris. It is only acceptable when focused local/mocked E2E
tests prove the workflow and report generation still falls back to deterministic
template/raw exports with no working LLM provider.

Before editing, state which canonical acceptance checkbox or `docs/end_goal.md`
stage the task advances. If the answer is "none", do not edit code. Pick the
smallest concrete kill-chain, validation, reporting fallback, dashboard review,
or test/cleanup gap instead.

If runtime `/goal` state, chat summaries, or historical handoffs disagree with
this section, treat them as stale. The goal lock and source-of-truth chain in
`END_GOAL.md`, `SPEC.md`, and `docs/end_goal.md` wins.

- [x] The UI/routing portion is not just a placeholder anymore: slug-based engagement routes, the detail workspace, graph explorer, report exports, audit timeline, raw-data preview, live seed management, and live run controls are all present and already covered by dashboard/API tests.
- [x] The core safe kill-chain path is real and verified: multi-seed persistence, recursive seed fan-out, artifact ingestion, deterministic cloud/key validation, deterministic finding synthesis, and report fallback all execute through the engagement-backed pipeline.
- [x] Task 11 is materially implemented and re-verified: deterministic template fallback, env-driven provider cascade, local-`llama_cpp` fallback, and raw JSON+CSV report-write degradation are all covered by focused Phase 6 plus end-to-end engagement-pipeline tests.
- [x] Report/export audit metadata now reaches the engagement detail experience too: both the generated dashboard detail JSON and the live `/api/engagements/{slug}` payload surface companion report metadata such as requested provider, rendered backend, exported backend, fallback reason, checksum, and raw-export status, and the React report panel renders that path directly.
- [x] Report/export auditability is tighter now too: the dashboard generator and live API both include `.csv` raw-export artifacts in the report family, `report_summary` now exposes `available_exports` plus `export_count`, the React detail panel renders that companion export family directly, and last-resort raw JSON+CSV fallback is visible end-to-end instead of appearing as a single JSON artifact.
- [x] Multi-generation reporting is clearer now too: the dashboard/API detail payloads now keep `report_summary` pinned to the latest report family, expose ordered `report_history` for older generations, the React detail route renders that history instead of mixing generations into one export list, and the static dashboard no longer mislabels report `.json`/`.csv` artifacts as graph artifacts just because of their suffix.
- [x] Live engagement seed classification is aligned with the backend mobile pipeline too: the web/API seed auto-detector now treats `.aab`, `.xapk`, `.apkm`, and `.apks` URLs as `apk_url`, so live engagement creation and seed CRUD match the CLI/orchestrator mobile-bundle path instead of downgrading those URLs into generic `url` seeds.
- [x] The Supabase mobile-key recovery path is aligned with that bundle support too: Phase 4 no longer limits mobile anon-key recovery to `.apk` / `.ipa` evidence, and now also consumes `.aab`, `.xapk`, `.apkm`, and `.apks` rows produced by the artifact/mobile extraction pipeline.
- [x] OpenDocument parser coverage is broader and actually re-verified now too: beyond the existing `.odt` path, focused artifact-queue regressions now prove `.ods` and `.odp` containers can surface emails, URLs, and cloud references into the deterministic seed/cloud pipeline instead of relying on suffix support without kill-chain evidence.
- [x] OpenDocument coverage is engagement-backed now too: a live local-artifact `kill_chain()` regression now proves `.ods` plus `.odp` artifacts can feed deterministic Firebase/Supabase/GCS/Azure validation, recursive email seed runs, attack-graph snapshot/export closeout, and template report generation in one engagement-backed run instead of stopping at artifact-queue-only coverage.
- [x] Mail-container parsing is less serialized now too: `.mbox` artifact extraction still preserves message order and metadata-first payload layout, but the expensive per-message parsing stage now uses the same bounded worker-pool model as other safe artifact substeps instead of serializing large mailboxes one message at a time.
- [x] Archive/container parsing is less serialized now too: zip/tar member payload extraction now uses the same bounded worker-pool model while preserving original member order, so larger nested archives no longer bottleneck on serial post-read member parsing.
- [x] Nested mobile bundle extraction is less serialized now too: outer archive members containing `.apk` / `.ipa` / `.aab` / `.xapk` / `.apkm` / `.apks` now use the same bounded worker-pool model while preserving original member order, so mobile static-analysis pivots inside larger archive drops no longer serialize member-by-member.
- [x] Payload-level cloud-config extraction is less serialized now too: once artifact/mobile text payloads are extracted, Firebase plus Supabase static extraction now uses the same bounded worker-pool model while preserving payload order, so larger text-heavy artifacts and mobile bundles no longer bottleneck on per-payload config scanning.
- [x] Payload-level text discovery collection is less serialized now too: once artifact/mobile text payloads are extracted, generic discovery precomputation for emails, phones, URLs, cloud refs, and key evidence now uses the same bounded worker-pool model while preserving payload order, so larger config-heavy artifacts no longer bottleneck on per-payload regex/context extraction before deterministic persistence.
- [x] Structured artifact discovery-job expansion is less serialized now too: `_persist_parsed_artifact()` now batches per-payload Terraform/JSON/key-value/YAML derivation through the same bounded worker-pool model before generic text-discovery collection, while preserving payload order and the existing deterministic persistence path for artifact-fed seeds.
- [x] Direct email-artifact part extraction is less serialized now too: single-message `.eml` / nested RFC822 attachment expansion now batches per-part attachment and nested-message extraction through the same bounded worker-pool model while preserving walk order and metadata-first payload layout.
- [x] SQLite and legacy OLE artifact parsing are less serialized now too: SQLite object extraction now fans out per table/view through read-only per-object connections, and legacy OLE stream processing now fans out after stream bytes are collected, both while preserving deterministic payload order.
- [x] MSG-specific OLE extraction is less serialized now too: after reading the OLE streams, MSG property-stream parsing and extracted attachment expansion now each run through bounded worker-pool stages while preserving original stream order, attachment order, and metadata-first payload layout.
- [x] HAR entry expansion is less serialized now too: once the HAR JSON is parsed, per-entry text shaping now runs through the bounded worker pool while preserving original entry order and the existing summary-first payload layout.
- [x] WARC record expansion is less serialized now too: once WARC record boundaries are identified, per-record header/body shaping now runs through the bounded worker pool while preserving original record order and the existing summary/body payload layout.
- [x] Embedded archive carving is less serialized now too: once buried archive offsets are identified inside legacy/RTF/OLE blobs, per-offset nested archive extraction now runs through the bounded worker pool while preserving original offset order and the existing carved-name scheme.
- [x] PostHog personal-key regional proof handling is tighter now too: the validator no longer stops at the first regional `200` response if the payload lacks a stable user identifier, and instead checks the next documented region before returning inconclusive. This keeps low-signal success payloads out of deterministic findings while still allowing a later region to provide stable proof.
- [x] Shared provider-ID false-positive handling is tighter now too: proof identifiers with static prefixes plus repeated placeholder suffixes are rejected by the live key validators and by Phase 4 validation-detail parsing, so prefixed scaffolds no longer become deterministic reportable proof.
- [x] Name-search recursive identity discovery is broader now too: targeted public-profile dorks were added for media, creator, presentation, learning, and film/photo profile families that the shared parser already supports, with mocked evidence that those dorks feed recursive username profile rows.
- [x] Windows event-log and trace artifacts now participate in passive static-analysis recursion: `.evtx`, `.evt`, and `.etl` classify as document artifacts, common event-log/trace MIME types recover safe suffixes for extensionless remote downloads, relative JS/manifest route detection recognizes linked event-log/trace artifacts, and top-level blobs feed the existing bounded binary-string path so carved emails, URLs, Firebase/Supabase refs, S3 buckets, and GCS buckets become recursive seeds/cloud assets without opening Event Viewer, importing logs, or using Windows Event Log APIs.
- [x] Windows execution-history artifacts now participate in passive static-analysis recursion: `.pf`, `.automaticDestinations-ms`, and `.customDestinations-ms` classify as document artifacts, common Prefetch / Jump List MIME types recover safe suffixes for extensionless remote downloads, relative JS/manifest route detection recognizes linked execution-history artifacts, and binary string carving feeds emails, URLs, Firebase/Supabase refs, S3 buckets, and GCS buckets into recursive seeds/cloud assets without parsing shell history stores with live Windows APIs.
- [x] Browser navigation/bookmark artifacts now participate in passive static-analysis recursion: extensionless Chromium-style `History`, `Archived History`, `Favicons`, `Top Sites`, and `Bookmarks` / `Bookmarks.bak` files classify as read-only SQLite or text config artifacts, SQLite MIME hints recover safe suffixes for extensionless downloads, and sampled navigation/bookmark rows feed emails, URLs, Firebase/Supabase refs, S3 buckets, and GCS buckets into recursive seeds/cloud assets without collecting cookie/password stores by default.
- [x] Browser WebCache artifacts now participate in passive static-analysis recursion: exact-pattern `WebCacheV*.dat` files classify as document artifacts, relative route detection recognizes linked WebCache artifacts, ESE MIME hints recover `.dat` for extensionless downloads, and top-level plus archive-contained blobs feed the bounded binary-string path without loading ESE databases or broadening arbitrary `.dat` collection.

This prevents ID reuse after deleted engagement DBs and preserves the one-DB-per-engagement layout.

- [x] Mobile bundle family extraction is less serialized now too: direct `apk` / `ipa` bundle parsing and nested non-archive mobile members now batch payload-text extraction plus Firebase and Supabase extractor families through the same ordered local worker-pool helper, so one bundle/member no longer walks those independent safe local readers strictly one-by-one before the existing ordered rebasing, payload-cloud expansion, and persistence phases.

- [x] PDF payload subextractors are less serialized now too: `_extract_pdf_payloads()` and `_extract_pdf_bytes_payloads()` now batch metadata scraping, XMP extraction, and OCR-family payload generation through the same ordered local worker-pool helper, so PDF parsing no longer walks those independent safe subextractors strictly one-at-a-time after page-level OCR already supports bounded parallelism.
- [x] HAR payload staging is less serialized now too: `_har_payload_tuples()` now batches summary generation and the existing per-entry extraction family through the ordered local worker-pool helper, so HAR parsing no longer builds its top-level summary block strictly before dispatching the already-bounded entry family when both are independent after JSON decode.
- [x] Plist/mobileconfig payload staging is less serialized now too: `_extract_plist_bytes_payloads()` now batches XML rendering and flattened-value extraction through the ordered local worker-pool helper after one plist parse, so plist-family artifacts no longer walk those two independent safe payload builders strictly one-by-one before the shared downstream discovery path.
- [x] SQLite payload staging is less serialized now too: `_extract_sqlite_connection_payloads()` now batches top-level object-summary generation alongside the existing bounded object-extraction family when the database can be safely reopened by path, so SQLite artifacts no longer emit `#sqlite-meta` strictly before dispatching the already-bounded table/view payload family in the common file-backed case.
